Fixes the dup leak and close logic like the reference, but returns early for '@' names before the reuse lookup, so reloads that keep an abstract socket would hit EADDRINUSE; it also adds unrelated listenerPool accounting, an Unwrap method and receiver changes.

The core fix is right: it closes the dup'd fd, unlinks via Addr() under the lock, and guards double close with a CAS; but the pre-listen unlink of abstract names is not guarded, so its own Linux abstract test would fail, and it makes deleteListener depend on a pointer field the reference does not need (hidden tests 0/7).

The core fix closely mirrors the reference (close the dup, lock during close, check the shared count pointer, unlink via Addr), but listen still unlinks a file named like an abstract socket, so its own abstract test would fail on Linux.

A focused fix that closes the leaked dup, unlinks the real address, detects double close via the underlying ErrClosed, uses a map-identity check so a racing listen keeps its file, and guards abstract names on both paths; one gap is that if holders close in reverse order the file can be left behind.

Closes the leaked dup, unlinks by address only when the closer is the registered holder, detects double close via ErrClosed and guards abstract names; one gap: when the last closer is not the map entry, the file is left behind.
